title: defects: budget action perpetual UPDATE, sso assignment ref crash, demo breaker role lacks perms
description:
## .what

three defects met while rhachet-roles-nheuron applied sso + a budget breaker on declastruct-aws
1.13.0 (declastruct 1.9.0, domain-objects 0.31.14), 2026-11-20.

## 1. budget action never converges (perpetual UPDATE)

declare `DeclaredAwsBudgetAction.definition.scp` with unique refs (policy `{ name }`, target
`{ email }`), apply, then re-plan: it reads UPDATE forever. the remote read returns primary refs
(policy `{ id: 'p-…' }`, target `{ id: '<account id>' }`); the diff counts the two ref forms of
one resource as a change. fix: hydrate the remote to the declared ref form (or compare refs by
identity). clamp: apply then re-plan reads KEEP.

## 2. sso account assignment refuses an extant remote

`DeclaredAwsSsoAccountAssignment.nested` types `permissionSet` and `principal` as the generic
`RefByUnique`. both refs carry a nested `instance` object the generic class does not declare, so
declastruct's diff + serialize throw `DomainObjectNotSafeToManipulateError` on any assignment
that already exists remote. it passes only when the principal ref comes from
`refByUnique(new DeclaredAwsSsoUser({...}))` — a full dobj built just to derive the ref. a
`RefByUnique.as(...)` or plain-literal principal fails. fix: declare the ref classes with their
nested shape (or nest the target dobj's ref).

## 3. the demo budget guards were never applied

`provision/aws.infra/account=demo/resources.budget.ts` `getResourcesOfBudgetGuards` ships a
breaker role with the trust policy only — budgets also needs `organizations:AttachPolicy` /
`DetachPolicy` to run the SCP action. defects 1 + 2 above are what the first live apply finds.
